main_body: Altar block: a white cloth/backdrop with a lavender cross panel (rows 11-23), a thin gold band (rows 24-25), a purple front face with a cross (rows 26-34), and a gray stone base step below.
top_band: No real top surface. Column x=16 runs from a white or lavender region (rows 11-23, L=255/170), which is a vertical cloth/panel with a cross, to a gold line at rows 24-25 (L=208/110), which is only a 1-2 row rim, then straight into the purple front face.
evidence: The large white region (rows 11-23) carries a cross panel and is a vertical face seen head-on, not a table top. The only candidate for a top is the gold line at rows 24-25, which is 1-2 rows (rim only). The purple front face has a flat cross painted on it, with no inset. The whole drawing is a front elevation with a thin gold rim, so it fails the 3/4 contract.

style.evidence: The measured facts show 25 distinct colours against 38-40 in the references, and 13 colours per tile against 17-20. Flat-fill coverage is 23%, against 13% and 0% in the references. The 13-row-tall white cloth area and the purple front are large flat fills with little grain or dither. The purple ramp has only about 3 steps (lavender, mid, dark purple). The gold and the gray stone base add some variety, and the outline is tinted (0% neutral), so it is not a sticker look. Overall it is flatter and thinner than the Beodeul references.
